bibl.title: When the Dead is laid the Grave
ܡܐ ܕܡܬܬܣܝܡ ܥܢܝܕܐ ܒܩܒܪܐ
bibl.author: John bar Aphtonia — ܝܘܚܢܢ ܒܪ ܐܦܬܘܢܝܐ

noteGrp.note: A funerary hymn, attributed by John bar Aphtonia, intended for the burial of the dead. It presents death as directing human hope away from temporal life towards the life to come, for which it petitions God to receive the departed servant.

note.quote: ܙ ܚ ܢܘܕܘܢ ܫܡܝܐ ܬܕܡܪܬܟ ܡܪܝܐ: ܡܐ ܪܘܪܒܢ ܘܡܐ ܬܗܝܪܢ ܬܕܡܪܬܟ ܕܠܘܬܢ ܡܪܝܐ.
VII VIII. The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O! Lord. How great and how marvellous are thy wonders toward us, Lord.
ܕܟܠܗ ܣܒܪܐ ܘܣܘܟܝܐ ܕܝܠܢ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܠܚܘܕ ܠܘܬ ܚܝܐ ܕܥܬܝܕܝܢ. ܠܗܢܘܢ ܕܐܫܘܐ ܠܡܫܟܚܘ: ܐܦ ܠܥܒܕܐ ܕܝܠܟ: ܡܪܝܐ ܛܒܐ ܐܦ ܪܚܡ ܐܢܫܐ:
And in order to show that all our hope and empectation is only on the future life; which admit thy bondman also to find, good and merciful Lord.
